### Review fixes (2026-11-06)

A review of the branch's diff made eight findings, seven of them distinct (two reviewers found the same `linksSeen` problem). Each was checked first, and all were real. Five were in the code and are fixed, with tests that fail before the fix and pass after. Two were in the tests: a check that could never fail, and a randomized run that checked bindings in only about a third of its runs. Those are fixed in the tests, and the behaviour they cover was right.

- **A copy gone for good no longer holds up full-screen elimination for the rest of Margin.app's run** (`WindowMatcher.swift`). "Every copy seen this session still reports" kept every link that ever reported, and the binder lives as long as Margin.app does. So after one profile's copy stopped for good (the socket guard, its background torn down, its last window closed, or Safari opened again with fewer profiles), no full-screen window was bound as "the only free window with its bounds" until Margin.app quit. A lone full-screen window then waited for its page or a focus change, and its copy was told "not drawn" after 1.5 s: the sidebar gone. Now each link has the time it last reported (kept fresh while it's held). It counts as away for `Timing.away` (5 s) after that, then it's forgotten. The list is cleared when the browser isn't running. A gone copy's windows that are still open are counted by their bounds (`serverHaving`), and missing ones by `missingFree`, as before. The 5 s keeps the case the rule was made for, a copy held and then let go while another's window is missing from the reads, never bound wrong. Tests: a copy gone with its window closed, then a new full-screen window bound after 5 s (it failed before: never bound); Safari quit and opened with one profile, bound at once (failed before). The older "B's copy seen and not reporting: still not" case still holds.
- **The front window and the Space change seen in one read are one transition** (the visible rule). A Space change was merged only into a front change seen before it. When one read saw both, the Space change came first, so the front change became a transition of its own, and the rule's threshold moved to the Space change plus 1 s. WebKit says the page is shown during or at the end of the slide, before that, and pages don't say it again. So the window was never bound by its page. In a real Safari log at 21:53:03 the front window changed 166 ms before macOS said the Space changed, and the Shell reads at once on that notice, so one read sees both. Now a front change whose "may have begun" time (the read before it) is at or before a Space change heard without one is folded into that transition, from the earlier time. A front change seen in a read after the one that saw the Space change is still a transition of its own, so a word between them isn't taken for it. Tests: both orders, in one read and across reads that told nothing (both failed before).
- **The randomized "pages" run now checks every run.** It checked bindings only in runs with every page saying and no Private window. Those are 293 of the 1000 runs. The other runs checked only "never wrong", and bound nothing at the end, because they ended with no focus change. Now those runs end with each window shown with its focus change, as Safari gives one when a window comes forward, and every full-screen window must be bound: 4000 of 4000 (1172 by the pages alone, 2828 with focus changes). The 40 Private-window runs end the same way and must bind all three reported windows. A new deterministic case covers three profiles with one page silent: the two that speak are bound as each is shown with its focus change. With a Private window, all three are bound. Behaviour is unchanged: with a silent page or a same-bounds Private window, the pages alone still bind nothing (never guessed), and a focus change does.
- **"No binding dropped for a window missing under 3 s" is measured.** It matched the drop line's words, and the line always says "(not listed for 3 s)", so the check could never fail. The test world now keeps when each window was last listed, and every drop for the window server must come at least `absent` after that. With `missing()` cut to 0.3 s, it fails in 40 of 50 runs (`window 102 dropped 1.10 s after it was last listed`).
- **A tab switch sends one or two `windows` reports, not three or four, and none of them wake the app's reads unless a window is unbound.** Each switch cleared the window's word and sent a report, then the new page's `visibilitychange` sent one and its answer to `reportVisibility` another (a new `visibleAt`). The old tab's "hidden" could also be sent as the window's, while the copy's last list still had it in front. Each report was pushed to every overlay of the link and set off a 1 s burst of window server reads and binder updates on Margin.app's main thread, the thread that handles the keys and the highlight. And each report's flags went to the log over the native port, with times that beat the dedupe. Now:
  - the same word again from a tab keeps its first time and sends nothing (`visibleAt` is "since when it has said so" now; PROTOCOL.md);
  - `tabActivated` puts the new tab in front in the copy's last list at once, so the tab left behind never speaks for the window;
  - the app passes a report that changes only `visible`/`visibleAt` to no overlay, and reads the window server for it once (not a burst) only while one of that copy's windows is unbound (`Shell.onlyVisibilityChanged`);
  - the flags line is written when the flags change (not their times) and at most once a second, as they are once the second is over.

  The `reportVisibility` ask on activation stays: it covers a page whose `visibilitychange` came before the activation and was cleared with it. Tests: `link.test.js` (the old tab's hidden never sent, the same word not sent, a change sent with its time, the flags line at most once a second), Swift `onlyVisibilityChanged`. The WebKit host's `visibility` scenario now reads the reports themselves (the link server's `windows` line carries each window's tab in front and word) instead of the flags line, which no longer has a line per report. Its checks are the same.
- **The highlight no longer goes back when Safari takes longer than 300 ms with a switch** (`shared/switching.js`). A passed tab in front counted as the chain's echo for `PASSED_MS` from when the state first had it. A Safari switch slower than that (450 ms) ended the chain on a passed tab while the newest target was still being carried out: `[1,14,13,…,5,14,4,3,9,4,3]`. Now the 300 ms start only once the newest target's request is answered. Until then a passed tab is the echo for up to `SETTLE_MS` (2 s), so a lost answer doesn't hold the highlight longer than that. Tests: the 12 fast presses with Safari at 350 to 600 ms a switch, and one at 1 s: the highlight never goes back and ends on the last press's tab, in one chain (it failed before). A unit case: held until the answer, then `PASSED_MS`, then followed; with no answer, followed after `SETTLE_MS`.
- **⌘T in the moments after a binding goes still opens something.** The copy hands ⌘T off while it thinks the app draws the window. That's until the app says "not drawn": 1.5 s for a window never bound, 3 s after a binding goes. It closes Safari's new tab and pushes the palette. The app held it 1.5 s and dropped it, and the user got neither a tab nor a palette. Now, when the app drops a held palette, it tells the copy "not drawn" at once (`DrawnOutbox.notShown`, past the grace). For ⌘T's hand-off (`newTab`) it also asks `paletteDropped`. The copy then opens Margin's new-tab page in that window and, for 10 s, keeps Safari's new tab and has its new-tab page show its own notice and address field, so the hand-off can't loop. That ends sooner when the app says it draws the window again, but not when it says so within a second of the drop: a binding that holds while its overlay can't show says it at once, and that mustn't start the hand-off and its drop again. The e2e check that locked in the silent drop now requires the `paletteDropped` request. `undrawn-window.test.js` plays it through the real background: the hand-off, the app's word, Margin's new-tab page opened, the next ⌘T's tab kept, still kept after a `drawn` at once, and handed to the palette after one a second later. Cost: about 1.5 s from ⌘T to the new-tab page in that case, the palette's hold.
- **Not changed:** the visible rule's gates (a silent page or an unreported same-bounds window still blocks it), the 1.5 s palette hold, the `drawn` graces otherwise.

### A page's own first paint no longer waits on Safari (2026-11-06)

The WebKit host's `first-paint` failed about one run in three after the iCloud Tabs merge: W0, the first fresh page after a new layout, drew its first frame at the registered 260/8 instead of its window's own 300/12. Its own sheet hadn't gone in yet. Each parent had passed 4 runs of 4, but with timings logged the reliability parent failed too (3 of 4), so the merge didn't cause it.

Timings logged per page: when the layout reached the background, `onCommitted`, `fixUp`'s window lookup, `insertCSS`, and the page's first frame. A page draws its first frame 17 to 21 ms after it commits. The background hears the commit 4 or 5 ms after it, so `fixUp` has about 12 ms.

- **The cause in Margin.** `fixUp` took the page's window from Margin's state and, when the state didn't have the new tab yet, asked Safari (`tabs.get`). That took 8 to 48 ms, longer than the time `fixUp` has. The sheet then went in after the first frame. Every run that had to ask failed (6 of 6), and it had to ask in 5 of the 8 merged runs. Real Safari would do the same, so a new tab could draw its first frames at the wrong inset in the two seconds after a layout change. Now `background/registered.js` keeps each tab's window from Safari's own events (`tabs.onCreated`, `onAttached`, `onActivated`, and the open tabs at start), so `fixUp` asks for the sheet in the same turn as the commit. It only asks Safari about a tab it has never heard of. Test: `undrawn-window.test.js`. A tab Margin's state doesn't have yet gets its own sheet in the commit's turn, and a moved tab gets its new window's. Without the fix this test fails.
- **The race in the test.** The host's `appLayout` step goes straight on to open W0, and the link server's `setLayout` took up to 200 ms to reach the background (usually 50 to 150). In the host, the background page runs its tasks (timers, the socket's messages) in turns about 200 ms apart: a 10 ms timer there fired every 210 ms. W0 commits about 95 ms after the layout is sent. With the fix above alone, 2 runs of 13 still failed because the layout arrived after the page committed. No code in Margin could have known it then. The scenario now waits until the copy has the layout before it opens W0 (`layoutLanded`). The check is unchanged.
- **Left as it is.** Twice in 28 pages, the background heard the commit late (11 and 46 ms) while none of Margin's code was running: its process was slow to wake. The sheet then missed the first frame. That's WebKit's timing, and it didn't happen in the 22 runs since.
- **Result.** `first-paint` passed 12 runs of 12 with no timing code, and 10 of 10 with it. Not changed: the registration's 2 s settle, and the `insertCSS` route itself.

### A window Margin.app stops drawing over: its new pages bare from the first frame (2026-11-06)

The WebKit host's `undrawn` failed U0 often (5 of 6 runs in the main checkout, 1 of 7 in another worktree): the fresh page in the window the app had just said it draws nothing over drew its first frames in the registered 260/8 box. It reproduces at will with the Mac busy (six busy loops: 3 of 4 failed).

- **Where the app's word waited.** Not in the link server, the socket or the host. With wall-clock stamps on both ends, the link server wrote `drawn` at once, and the copy's background read it 2 to 190 ms later when the Mac was quiet, 2 s later in the failing logs. The background page's WebContent process runs at background priority (`ps`: priority 4, the visible page's 47), since it shows no page. A 50 ms timer in it fired every 250 ms, and the socket's message was read within 15 ms of one of those wakes in each of 6 runs. With other work on the Mac it got no time at all for up to seconds. That's WebKit's own throttling of a process with no visible page, likely the same in Safari (not checked there). Turning off WebKit's hidden-page timer throttling and process suppression for the background (private preferences on the controller's configuration) changed nothing.
- **Why the first frame was boxed.** Until the registration followed (`LAYOUT_SETTLE_MS`, 2 s after the change), a new page in that window depended on `fixUp`: `--margin-fp: off` put in as it commits, which must land within the 17 to 21 ms before its first frame. With the background that slow, it landed 30 to 70 ms after the commit, after one or two boxed frames (logged per page: commit, `onCommitted` heard, `fixUp`, sheet in, each frame). So the product was wrong, not the test: on a busy Mac, a page opened within 2 s of leaving full screen could show the box and its grey frame for a frame or two.
- **Now.** A change in what the app draws is followed at once (`registered.js windowDrawnChanged`; `background.js` onDrawn), not after the settle. The app already sends `drawn` only as it changes, and off only after its grace (1.5 to 3 s, `DrawnOutbox`), so a binding that comes and goes doesn't re-register faster than a settling layout does. The registration reads the link's own word while this copy is linked (`appLink.view()`), since storage gets it 120 ms later. Pages in the window from then on are bare from their first frame however slow the background is. A layout with no box anywhere (the frame turned off) now registers at once too (`layoutsChanged`); one with a box still waits the 2 s, as a sidebar drag sends many. The host's `hidden-box` showed why: once the registration read the link's own layouts, a page reloaded 0.4 s after the frame went off started the registered 8 px box and needed its commit's `off` sheet (2 runs of 3). It had passed before only because the settings change's sync read storage before the first layout was written there, found none, and fell back to the settings' (no frame: no box). `fixUp` is still the only way for a window that differs from most (several windows, some not drawn), and that stays a race on a busy Mac. The content script's log no longer says "Margin.app draws Margin around this window" in a window the app said it draws nothing over: it says it's linked but draws nothing there (only the log line was wrong; the box was already none).
- **Tests.** `tests/undrawn-window.test.js`: the registration goes to zeros at once when the window becomes undrawn, while storage still has the old word, and back to the box at once when it's drawn again (it can't pass with the settle, or with the registration read from storage); a layout with no box registered at once, one with a box not. The host's `undrawn` now checks that the registration followed within 1.5 s (WebKit gives the new registration's CSS to the open page too, so its variables show it) before U0 opens. U0 then checks no box, no mark and none of Margin's page scripts.
- **Left as it is.** A window's own layout in the 2 s after a change with a box still depends on its commit's sheet: `first-paint`'s W0 or W1 missed its first frame in 2 of 10 runs on this build and 1 of 6 on the build before, the same race. Following such layouts at once would undo the settle that keeps a sidebar drag from piling registrations up; not changed.
- **A box back after none, at once too (review).** Registering a layout with no box at once, but a box only after the settle, made a quick Keep open off and on with the frame off worse: before, the registered box stayed through it; now zeros went in at once and the box only 2 s after it came back. While zeros are registered `fixUp` puts in nothing (it only gives a window its own layout beside a registered box), so pages opened then started with no box beside the sidebar and jumped into it once the page heard the layout. So a box back in a layout whose zeros were registered only for want of a box (linked, shown) is followed at once as well (`registered.js noBoxForLayout`); a box after another box still waits. Tested in `tests/undrawn-window.test.js` (fails on the build before).
- **Result.** `undrawn` passed 12 runs of 12 (5 of 5 with six busy loops beside it, where the build before failed 3 of 4), `first-paint-off` 4 of 4, `hidden-box` 3 of 3, every host scenario in one run.
- **A lone layout change at once (later the same day).** The W0/W1 race above is gone for one window: `layoutsChanged` registers a layout change at once when none came in the 2 s before it (`background/settle.js settler`), and a burst (a sidebar drag) registers its first at once at most, then only the layout it settles at, 2 s after its last change. The settled one is chosen once any registration under way is done, from the layouts as they are then, so a burst that came back to where it was doesn't end at the value a slow registration was writing. With windows at different layouts the registered one is still `chooseLayout`'s (most windows', a tie keeping it): a change that doesn't tip it registers nothing, and that window's new pages still depend on `fixUp`'s sheet, a race on a busy Mac. So does a page opened in the ~100 ms between a change reaching the background and its registration landing. `first-paint` now checks the registration followed within 1.8 s (the build before fails it, and W0) and that a drag ends at its last layout; W's pages come from the registration. 12 of 12 runs, 4 of 4 with six busy loops; `first-paint-off`, `undrawn`, `hidden-box` 4 of 4 each.
- **A burst's no-box cases judged after the registration under way (review).** In a burst, "no box anywhere" and "a box back after none" were judged against `registeredKey`/`noBoxForLayout` as they were when the change came, not what a registration still being written would leave: Keep open off (lone: zeros start registering) and on again before those zeros were in left them registered, with no fix-up, until the settle 2 s later, so new pages started bare beside the sidebar. `layoutsChanged` now judges those cases once any registration under way is done (at once when none is), and skips the check when another sync was queued meanwhile (it reads the layouts as they are then). The new test in `tests/undrawn-window.test.js` fails on the build before; it also covers the burst's no-box path, which the earlier test stopped reaching once its first change became a lone one.

### Every profile links again after Margin.app restarts (2026-11-06)

Seen at 20:35: after `npm run safari` relaunched Margin.app, only the Work profile linked again. Test A, Test B, Test and Personal never asked again for over 10 minutes: not when a page loaded there, and not from the toolbar button.

- **How it was found.** Notes were added to a build, which was then installed on real Safari 27.2 (macOS 27.2). They logged the handler getting each `wantLink`, each copy's `sendNativeMessage` answer, each `link` and `appUp` each copy heard, and pokes. Five copies started within 20 ms (Safari reloads every profile's copy for an update). The handler got all five `wantLink`s, each in its own handler instance on the main thread. **Only the last one (Work's) got an answer.** The other four `sendNativeMessage` promises never settled; they were still open 12 minutes later. Every copy heard **every** dispatch: all five `link`s (each copy took its own nonce's) and the `appUp`. The four copies were stuck in `ask()`, which waits for the answer before taking its `link`. So `busy` stayed set forever: no retry timer, and `appUp`, page pokes and `askNow` all saw a try under way and did nothing. Earlier that evening the copies started a second or so apart and all linked.
- **Not the cause.** Dispatches don't go to one profile only. Every copy heard each one, whichever window was in front. The backgrounds weren't suspended either: they kept noting things, and heard `appUp` while stuck.
- **The fix (`background/link.js`).** The copy waits at most 3 s for the handler's answer (`REPLY_WAIT_MS`). It takes its `link` as soon as it comes, answered or not. A copy without Safari's id for its profile (none kept from an earlier answer) still waits for the answer before its hello. An answer that has no id at all (the WebKit host's handler) counts as Safari's word that none will come. If that answer is lost, it asks again. No answer and no link: it asks again after 5 to 7.5 s, spread a little, three times, then the doubling. Anything that asks while a try is under way (`appUp`, a page starting, Start, Try again) makes the copy ask again as soon as that try ends unlinked. A try under way 45 s is left (`STUCK_MS`). Each 20 s ping checks that an unlinked copy has a try under way or one to come. The protocol and the app are unchanged (`app/PROTOCOL.md` steps 1, 2 and 8 updated).
- **Not chosen: the link in the handler's answer.** The app would write `{ port, token, key }` into the extension's container, and the handler would give it back in its answer. But the answer is the very part Safari loses, while the dispatch reaches every copy. It would also put the token on disk, with no gain. The token still goes only through `dispatchMessage`, never in the distributed notification.
- **Checked on real Safari (Test A and Test B, five profiles' copies running).** Installing the fixed build reloaded every copy at once: all five linked within 3.5 s. Four lost answers were logged, and each copy took its link anyway. Margin.app quit (SIGTERM, `bye`) and opened again three times: with Test A's window in front, 5 of 5 linked 0.8 s after the start; with Test B's in front, 5 of 5 in 0.8 s; with another app in front, 4 in 1.1 s and the fifth in 3.6 s (its first ask had no answer and no link). Quit for 25 s: the copies' 5 s ask started Margin.app through the handler, and all five linked within 3.3 s.
- **Tests.** `tests/link-relink.test.js` (7) uses a fake Safari that answers only the last of a burst of native messages and sends every dispatch to every copy. It covers: five copies starting at once, each linking as its own profile; an answer that never comes and no link (asked again on the schedule, no busy loop); `appUp`, a page or the person while a try waits on a lost answer; a stuck try left; a copy without Safari's profile id; and five copies after `bye` and `appUp`. All 7 fail (time out) on the code before the fix. A new WebKit host scenario, `app-link-lost`, has the host pass `wantLink`s on to the real link server but never answer them (`appLoseAnswers`). The real extension links again from the dispatched link as a page starts. Before the fix it never did (two FAILs).

## Margin 2: iCloud Tabs (2026-11-05)

On `feat/icloud-tabs` (from `feat/margin-app` at e3725be). Requested on 2026-11-05: "It should show up in the sidebar as a live folder above the new tab stuff, and should have a good UI/UX as well, and also show up in the command palette for now." Margin shows the tabs open in Safari on the person's other Apple devices, read from Safari's own file by Margin.app, in a live folder in each Safari window's sidebar and as a section of the palette.

**What Safari keeps** (read on a real Mac with Margin.app's permission: the schema, row counts, metadata keys, the device types and the position blob's format; never a title, an address or a device's name):
- `~/Library/Containers/com.apple.Safari/Data/Library/Safari/CloudTabs.db`, SQLite in WAL mode: `cloud_tab_devices` (4 rows), `cloud_tabs` (21), `cloud_tab_close_requests` (0), `metadata` (only `use_manatee_container` and `server_change_token`).
- **This Mac's own record:** nothing in `metadata` (or in Safari's preferences: its device identifiers have moved to the keychain, `DidMigrateDeviceIdentifier …`) says which device is this Mac. Two device rows have this Mac's name (its computer name) and its model (`com.apple.macbookpro-14-2021-space-gray`, a 14-inch 2021 MacBook Pro, `MacBookPro18,3`), both with no tabs. So a device is taken to be this Mac when it's a Mac named as this Mac is (`SCDynamicStoreCopyComputerName`), and a device with no tabs isn't shown either (as in Safari). Limit: a Mac renamed keeps its old name in Safari's row until Safari writes it again; another Mac with exactly this Mac's name would be hidden too.
- **The position blob:** zlib (78 DA header, deflate, Adler-32) around JSON, `{"sortValues":[{"changeID":0,"sortValue":-689,"deviceIdentifier":"<uuid>"}]}`. Every tab's `deviceIdentifier` was different (one per insert), and on one device the values ran 201, 1201, 1424, 2201, 2424, … : a fractional-index position, compared value by value (the number, then the identifier), a shorter list before a longer one it begins. A tab whose position doesn't read goes after those that do, newest viewed first (`last_viewed_time`).
- **`device_type_identifier`:** `com.apple.iphone-13-pro-9`, `com.apple.macbookair-15-2025-silver`, `com.apple.macbookpro-14-2021-space-gray`: Apple's model identifiers. `iphone`/`ipod` → iPhone, `ipad` → iPad, `vision`/`realitydevice` → Vision, `mac` → Mac, anything else a generic device (globe icon).
- **Times:** `last_modified` is rounded to the local day (all four were at a local midnight); `last_viewed_time` is to the second. "updated …" uses the newest tab viewed when that's newer, to the minute ("updated 5 min ago"), else the record's day ("updated yesterday").
- **Ephemeral and duplicate names:** none on a real Mac (both flags 0, even for the two rows with the same name). An ephemeral device is shown like any other if it has tabs; a name that's Safari's duplicate (its flag) or the same as another shown device's gets the kind after it ("Studio (Mac)", then "Studio (Mac 2)").
- **Profiles:** there's one `CloudTabs.db` for all of Safari; no profile folder has one. Named profiles do have their own per-device rows in `SafariTabs.db` (`bookmarks`, `subtype` 3 for this device and 4 for others, under the profile's row, each holding windows of tabs), but on a real Mac the other devices' entries there were nearly empty (one blank tab). **Decided:** the folder shows `CloudTabs.db`, the same in every Safari window whatever its profile. It's what "iCloud Tabs" means on every device, and it's predictable. Reading each named profile's own other-device lists from `SafariTabs.db` is a possible later step, once its format is seen with real data.

**How it's built:**
- **The app reads, never the extension** (`app/shell/CloudTabs.swift`). `SafariFiles.swift` now holds what the profile names and iCloud Tabs share: the access check (a read attempt), the read-only open (`SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY`, `mode=ro`, `immutable=1` when there's no `-wal`, 200 ms busy timeout; Margin never writes, vacuums or checkpoints), and the watcher (kqueue on the database and its `-wal`, FSEvents on the folder, a read at most once a second, the outcome handed on only when it changed), which `SafariProfileWatcher` now uses too. iCloud Tabs' watcher also skips a read when both files have the size, time and inode of the last good read.
- **To the overlays directly** (`ShellCloudTabs.swift`): in each Safari overlay's hello and as `{ type: 'cloudTabs' }` when it changed, the way `across` goes (`app/PROTOCOL.md` "iCloud Tabs"). The reads run only while a Safari copy is linked with the setting on.
- **In the UI:** `extension/shared/cloud-tabs.js` checks what came (ids, web addresses only, caps) and has Margin's words; `ui/view-model.js` builds `cloudTabs` (structural sharing keeps every unchanged row the same object, so a live update redraws only what changed and the list keeps its scroll); the runtime makes the model again once a minute while devices are shown, for "updated … ago".
- **Theme API:** a new slot, `<m-cloud-tabs>`, showing a new part, `cloud-tabs`, while `cloudTabs` is set. The part draws the whole folder on its own, so it can later be shown elsewhere (the "icon beside the sidebar's toggle" idea, `PLAN.md` §13) with no theme change. It's a guarded part: every word in it is Margin's, since its one button asks for a permission. New actions: `cloud.toggle`, `cloud.toggleDevice`, `cloud.open`, `cloud.copy`, `cloud.access`; palette rows gained `section` and `sectionStart`. Documented in `extension/themes/README.md`.
- **Look:** Arcadia draws it as one of Arc's folders with a sky-blue cloud in the folder icon's place, a count and a turning chevron, quiet device headings (icon, name, "updated …" in small grey), two-line rows (title over site), a divider under it. Neo-brutalism draws a bordered card with a sky-blue head and a cloud, each device a black tag with its icon and name (white when folded, dashed when stale), two-line rows with the site in small caps, and a yellow pin badge.
- **Where:** above the new-tab row, outside every drop zone (Arcadia: between the pinned area's divider and the tab list; Neo-brutalism: between the folders and the today zone). No `m-drag` or `m-drop` in it.
- **Collapse:** the folder and each device fold; kept in settings (`cloudTabsOpen`, `cloudTabsClosed`: Safari's device ids, devices gone are dropped as one is toggled), so it lasts and is the same in a profile's windows; shown at once, before storage comes back.
- **Click:** opens the address as one typed in the palette does: `newTab { windowId, url }` (this window, its space), or in place over Margin's new-tab page. There are no Cmd-click or middle-click conventions in the sidebar to follow, so none were added.
- **Menu:** Open and Copy Link (`copyText`, the app's pasteboard). Open in New Window isn't offered: `newWindow` takes no address, and adding one would change an existing request.
- **States:** no other devices with tabs ("No tabs are open on your other devices."), no Full Disk Access (one row and a button that opens System Settings at Full Disk Access, the URL the set-up window's step opens, now shared as `SafariFiles.fullDiskAccessURL`), no file ("No iCloud Tabs yet…"), a database that isn't Safari 27.2's ("couldn't read"). A device not used for 7 days is dimmed.
- **Icons:** Margin's stored icon for the site's origin (`state.favicons`), else a letter on a color. No request is made for them.
- **The palette:** iCloud tabs show only once something is typed (before typing: none, as recent ones weren't asked for). They come as their own section **after Margin's own rows (open tabs, pins, actions, the archive) and before "Search for …"** (an address typed still puts "Open …" first). Why there: the palette ranks Margin's own kinds on one score, and a section has to stay together; putting it after them never pushes the person's own tabs down and leaves the existing order exactly as it was, while a match on another device is still more specific than a web search. One run per device, headed "On <device>", the device with the best match first (as good a match: the one used most recently), at most 5 per device and 8 in all. A page already open in this window isn't offered again from another device.
- **Settings:** "Show iCloud Tabs: the tabs open on your other devices, in the sidebar and the command palette", on by default, right after the frame setting (Settings has no sidebar heading; adding one would move the existing fields). Only in Margin.app's Safari windows. Off, the app stops reading.
- **The set-up window's** Full Disk Access step now says Margin reads the tabs open on the person's other devices too (its title: "Show Safari's profile names and iCloud Tabs").
- **Privacy:** the app's log says counts only; tests use databases they make in a temporary folder and never read Safari's path (the folder is an option; nil in the harness); the scratch copies used for the research were deleted.

**Limits:** read only (Margin never writes Safari's files); no closing a tab on another device (`cloud_tab_close_requests` is Safari's); no favicons from Safari (the database has none); this Mac found by its name; profiles all see the same iCloud Tabs; Safari only for now (Chrome and Edge in Phase 5 through `sessions.getDevices()`, `PLAN.md`).

**Not done:** a WebKit host scenario (the host runs the extension, not the app's overlay, and iCloud Tabs never pass through the extension; the app's end-to-end test draws the folder in the real overlay instead); recent iCloud tabs in the palette before typing; the icon beside the sidebar's toggle (`PLAN.md` §13, later).

**Tests.** Unit (`npm test`) 696 (15 new: `tests/cloud-tabs.test.js` 14 and a guard test; three tests that list the actions, guarded parts and features extended). Theme (`npm run test:theme`) 108 (32 new: `tests/theme/cloud.test.js`, both themes in WebKit and Chromium: the folder above the new-tab row and outside drop zones, clicks, the menu, collapse, a live update touching one row's text and keeping the scroll, the no-permission row, the setting, the palette's section and Enter). App (`npm run test:app`) 513 unit checks (`tools/app-tests/cloud-tabs-tests.swift`: order, fallback, this Mac left out, empty devices, web pages only, kinds, a busy database, no permission, a missing file, Safari closed with nothing made beside the file, a file that isn't Safari's, a database changed while open, the watcher following the log with few reads, a read skipped when nothing changed, the permission withdrawn and given back, what's sent and what's logged) and 185 end-to-end (11 new, `e2e-cloud.swift`: a stand-in file drawn live in the real overlay, a row's press asking the copy for a new tab, the setting stopping the reads, the Full Disk Access row and its button), no compiler warnings with the Xcode target's settings.

**Open:** the `TESTING.md` checks ("Margin 2: iCloud Tabs"), first that this Mac isn't listed and that each device's order matches Safari's.


## The e2e suite rewritten (2026-11-06)

On `test/e2e-rewrite` (from `feat/margin-app`). The request: the e2e suite rewritten, on pages that look and behave like real sites. The plan is `docs/e2e-plan.md`; `TESTING.md` "The e2e suite" says how to run it.

**What runs.** The Safari build's profile in headless Chromium, linked through a native messaging relay to a stand-in Margin.app in Node; the real overlay page in headless WebKit; a local site of 20 realistic pages on 17 `.test` sites. Nothing leaves the Mac.

**The second half** (plan items 11 to 17):

- `sleep.test.js` (4): a pass closes idle pages and keeps their Margin tabs, not open; a mail draft, the podcast and the video playing, a never-sleep site, text in another site's frame and the tab in front stay; a click opens one again; off the list, the dashboard sleeps.
- `page-box.test.js` (8): every site in the slot at the slot's width, with a picture of each; `?fp` pages in the box from their first frame; Keep open, a peek and a wider sidebar; the docs' media queries and `vw`; the travel page's fixed bar, sticky sub-nav, cookie bar, chat bubble and modal; frames; no box where the app doesn't draw.
- `scroll.test.js` (9, rewritten): the wheel and a sticky bar; the feed loading more; scroll kept across switches; no bounce; sideways swipes stopped, not over a carousel, and the setting; pull to refresh and swipe drawn by the overlay; none when scrolled down, small, toward no history, or off.
- `loading.test.js` (5): a report streaming in; leaving a page shown before a slow server answers; a reload; a 204; a mail draft's "Leave page?".
- `cloud-tabs.test.js` (8): the folder above New Tab, devices folded, a tab opened here, Copy Link and Full Disk Access asked of the app, the palette's section, the setting.
- `data.test.js` (4): the app's set as the cache; changes sent as made; changes made while the app was gone, in the next `data.hello`; a wiped profile filled again.
- `link-drops.test.js` (5): a drop mended in about 0.3 s; the app gone a moment (dimmed, "Reconnecting", box kept) and back; gone past 6 s (no box, the new-tab notice) and a new app; a goodbye; a wrong welcome key.
- `themes.test.js` (1 + 1 per theme): each theme in `PACKAGE_THEMES` chosen in the Settings of the one before, sent again, and drawn with tabs, pins, a folder, iCloud Tabs, the palette, the launcher's archive, a menu, the editor, a notice, the hidden sidebar and a peek. Pixel joins on its own once Phase 6 lists it.
- `chrome-build.test.js` (6): `dist/chrome` alone: it starts, its new-tab page, Chrome's shortcuts and icons, nothing in pages, `chrome.search`.

**Harness changes:**

- Headless Chromium shows every tab as visible. A script the background runs in a tab behind the front one now sees it hidden while it runs (`build.js` `HIDDEN_BEHIND`), as Safari's would be. Without it no tab ever sleeps.
- The relay answers `wantLink` with Safari's id for the profile (`s-default`), as `SafariWebExtensionHandler.swift` does. The stand-in app has a set only for that profile; any other gets `data.need`.
- The shell can `kill()` the app (nothing listening) and `restart({ welcome })`. `m.worker` follows a background that starts again.
- The site: `?wait=<ms>` answers late, `?nocontent` answers 204, on any address.

**The old suite.** `enhancements`, `loader`, `platform`, `scroll` and `smoke` went with `helpers.js`. Their tests are in `scroll`, `navigation`, `loading` and `chrome-build`. One was dropped: upgrading to the Safari build moves the ⌃⌘ shortcut defaults. `tests/model.test.js` covers it, and stopping Chromium's worker tests nothing Safari does.

**Bugs found, kept as `todo`** (nine in all; the first four are the first half's, noted in their files; seven fixed since, below, two left: the new-tab page's link bugs):

- `newtab.html#launcher` gets no launcher, and the page says "Margin.app isn't running" while linked (`archive`, `newtab`).

**Fixed since** (`fix/e2e-found-bugs`; each test is a normal one now):
- Arcadia's notice a word per line: `width: max-content` under its `max-width` (`themes`).
- An extension id shown as a host: `face()` in `ui/view-model.js` gives Margin's own pages no host, so the address field is empty and a kept start page gets its title's letter (`themes`, `tests/ui-view-model.test.js`).

- The new-tab page's hidden notice was drawn while linked: `main { display: grid }` beat `[hidden]`. `newtab.html` now has `[hidden] { display: none !important }` (`newtab`; unit: `newtab-page`).
- A tab open before the app's set came in kept the default space the set removed, and no row showed it. `stateFromDataSet` (`shared/data-set.js`) now moves a tab whose space the set took away to its window's space, or the first (`tabs`; unit: `data-set`).
- The iCloud Tabs folder pressed twice before the app's word came back stayed closed: the next press's request was made from the stored state. `ui/runtime.js` dispatch now makes requests from `viewState` (what's drawn), for the folder, a device's fold and Keep open alike (`cloud-tabs`; theme harness: `tests/theme/cloud.test.js`).
- `vw` inside a `font` shorthand that also has a `var()` wasn't moved to the box: its longhands read empty while the `var()` is pending. `shiftStyle` (`shared/page-css.js`, used by `content/page/sheets.js` for rules and style attributes) now sets such a shorthand again as a whole, putting back the longhands set apart from it (`page-box`; unit: `page-css`).
- A body with a gradient background was drawn wrong in the box (Chromium: a step at the box's width and a band along its bottom). With nothing on `<html>`, `<body>`'s background is the canvas's, laid out at `<html>`'s size from the window's corner. `content/page/box.js` (`checkBackground`, the CSS from `shared/page-box.js` `bodyBackgroundCss`) now gives `<html>` a background with no weight when `<body>`'s has an image, so it stays on `<body>`, which fills the box; the canvas keeps `<body>`'s color. WebKit drew the box right before but tiled the gradient outside it; a body with a transparent color now shows the default canvas there (`page-box`; unit: `page-css`; WebKit host: `body-background`).

**Seen, not a bug:** with `storage.local` wiped but `storage.session` kept, the background links on its kept link and never asks the handler, so it says hello under a profile id of its own making. Safari wipes both at once (the extension loads again), so the test wipes both.

**Review fixes** (the suite only; no product change):

- Every file now fails on a leak, an overlay load from the web or an overlay error: `m.close()` checks all three. Before, four files checked `m.leaks` and three the overlay.
- "A switch by hand starts a new chain" presses inside the chain's 1.5 s, so it fails without the reset. The new-tab page's next-tab key has a test.
- Checks that only read the stand-in shell now read the copy's stored link state (`appLink`: off, nothing drawn; a window drawn).
- Deleting a space deletes one with a tab: the tab and the window go to the first space.
- The site: the dashboard's KPI cards stay in their columns (the site test checks no grid item spills); the shop's filters are all off, so the grid matches them.
- Pictures: the notice is waited out before the next theme's, and the peek and wide sidebar are taken after their transitions.
- Sleep: "one row, not two" no longer counts rows by title after a fixed pause (it saw 0 once under load).
- Start on the new-tab page waits for the copy's link to start before the press. Once, under load, the press came first: the page said "Margin can't reach Margin.app from here" (`askNow` is false until the copy owns the state), then "didn't answer, try again" at once. A second press works. Worth a look later: the page could wait for the link instead.

**Not covered here:** the window server, Spaces, pass-through and hot keys; WebKit's extension engine; the app's files and its Swift link. `npm run test:app` and `npm run test:webkit` have them.

**Time.** The whole suite: 129 and 131 s in two runs on a real Mac, the build included (target: under 4 minutes). 119 tests: 113 pass, 6 `todo`, none skipped. After the review: 123 tests, 114 pass, 9 `todo`, none skipped; 132 s in each of three runs in a row (138 to 205 s while the Mac was busy with other work, load 15 to 44).

## Margin 2, Phase 6 plan: Pixel, Neo-brutalism, user themes (2026-11-06)

On `feat/pixel-user-themes`. The plan is `docs/phase6-themes.md`; the boards, a renderer for them (`tools/boards/`) and reference shots are in `docs/phase6/`. Choices the plan makes, to confirm before they're built:

- **User themes belong to the Mac, not a profile.** Margin.app keeps each one in `~/Library/Application Support/Margin/themes/<id>.json` with an index. Each profile's data set gets only the index (`userThemes`, a few hundred bytes), never a package: a package can be 4.5 MB, over the link's 1 MB cap.
- **Import goes through the app.** The overlay can't open a file picker, so Settings asks the app (`perform theme.import`), which shows `NSOpenPanel` over full screen and reads a folder or a `.margintheme` zip within the package caps. The checks run once, in JS, with the same code as every load: the zip is read in the overlay, not in Swift.
- **Preview before use,** under a bar of Margin's own in the top layer that no theme can style or cover, and that cancels by itself after 30 s.
- **Arcadia is the fallback,** bundled with the app's overlay, for a theme that's refused, missing, or leaves no usable page. Removing the active theme puts Arcadia back in every profile that used it.
- **User themes get a plain first paint** (the box, nothing around it), not Arcadia's frame.
- **Pixel and Neo-brutalism keep one look in both system modes,** as their boards have one each.
- **A space's number** (`number`, from 1) joins the view model, for Pixel's "WORLD 2-1" and numbered chips; templates have no arithmetic.
- **Bundled SVG images stay unsanitized:** they're only ever drawn as images (an `img` or a CSS image), where WebKit runs no script and loads nothing. A payload test keeps that true.
- **`npm run test:security`** gathers the sanitizer, guard, package and import payloads, every built-in theme, and any packages named in `MARGIN_THEMES`. No CI is added; the plan says how a macOS runner would run it later.

## Margin 2, Phase 6: the first review of themes (2026-11-06)

On `feat/pixel-user-themes`. Fourteen findings; all fixed but parts of the last.

- **The theme choice shows its status** in all three built-ins (why Margin fell back to Arcadia). The guide's example draws `status` under a choice and a button.
- **The theme's own settings come after Margin's,** right before "Keyboard shortcuts". Import Theme… and the imported themes stay under the theme choice. Margin's rows no longer sit under "Settings of “Name”".
- **An imported theme's id survives every fresh read.** `normalizeState` keeps any id an imported theme may have (`USER_THEME_ID`, the same rule as `ThemeStore.idOK`). It doesn't read the index: Margin.app, the overlay and Settings already fall back to Arcadia for an id that isn't listed. Earlier names of a built-in (`arcadium`, `arcadia-2`) still become it.
- **A zip entry of a kind no package holds is refused before it's inflated.** Every inflate stops at the least of its declared size, its kind's cap and what's left of the 3 MB package. A 1 GB entry in a small zip is refused at once.
- **The overlay remembers what it draws,** Arcadia standing in included. Cancel, Escape, the 30 s timeout and a preview that fails put that back (Arcadia as the fallback again, still saying why).
- **Use Theme keeps the theme from before until the app's package comes.** A refusal (`themeSaved` not ok), a package that can't be stored, or no package within 10 s put it back. Settings says "Saving…", then "Saved.", or why not. No change in `app/shell`.
- **The fallback package is read only as the script's own property** of the window, with its shape checked, and a bad result isn't cached. The sanitizer removes `marginFallbackTheme` and any id that is `margin` and then a letter, digit or `_` (Margin's globals are named so; Arcadia's `margin-results` stays).
- **An imported theme must have its ways back out:** the `launcher`, `settings`, `prompt` and `notice` parts, `<m-launcher>`, `<m-prompt>` and `<m-notice>` in the window's tree, and `<m-settings>` in the launcher part. The sanitizer reports where parts and slots are; `checkImport` refuses one that lacks them and says what's missing. Built-in themes aren't held to it (they have them all).
  - **Not covered:** a theme can still hide those with CSS. The preview shows it first, under Margin's own bar. The set-up window's "Use Arcadia in every profile" is still to build.
- **Neo-brutalism's palette tags** take the row's own space's colour (`spaceColor` in the view model; white for Archived, Search, Open, iCloud), and all have one width (92 px), so the icons and titles line up.
- **Search and Open rows have drawn icons** in Neo-brutalism and Pixel (`isSearch`, `isOpen` in the view model): the fonts' ⌕ and ↗ drew as specks.
- **Neo-brutalism's loose pins** line up with folder rows (4 px plus the folder's 2.5 px border).
- **Many spaces:** Neo-brutalism's chips keep 34 px and scroll sideways; Pixel's keep their size, stay centred while they fit (`safe center`) and scroll inside the bar.

## Margin 2, Phase 6: user themes and the security suite (2026-11-06)

Work items 2 and 7 to 10 of `docs/phase6-themes.md`, on `feat/pixel-user-themes`.

### The security suite

- **One command: `npm run test:security`.** It runs the sanitizer and guard payloads, the new payloads (`tests/security/`), every built-in theme through the checks an import goes through, and the live part in WebKit and Chromium (`tests/theme/security.test.js`). The Node parts stay in `npm test`, the live part in `npm run test:theme`.
- **`MARGIN_THEMES`** (folders, `:` between them) adds a theme of anyone's to the same checks, before it's shared.
- **New rules, found by the new payloads:**
  - An svg `<use>` inside a guarded part is removed. It could draw svg `<text>` from a `<symbol>` outside the part: theme words in a menu.
  - Ids named like the globals Margin's code reads (`browser`, `chrome`, `webkit`, `marginApp`, `Margin`, `T`, `top`…, any case) are removed. The overlay's container is its document, so a theme's ids are the window's names; `shared/platform.js` reads `globalThis.browser ?? globalThis.chrome`.
  - A second template for one part is removed (the renderer uses the first; a second is a decoy).
  - `checkPackage` checks each file's first bytes against its kind, and refuses two paths that differ only by case (one file on the Mac's disk).
  - `theme.json` with a key twice in one object is refused (`JSON.parse` keeps the last; a reader that takes the first sees another id). Names, authors and labels with bidi controls or zero-width characters are refused.
- **Kept on purpose:** a `data:` font in `@font-face` loads nothing and stays capped at 128 KB, so it stays allowed (fonts in `theme.json` remain the way the README teaches).
- **The overlay's policy is tested on its own:** a page served with `OverlaySchemeHandler.policy` (read from the Swift source) and every payload put in raw, with no sanitizer, runs none of them and makes no request. A control run without the policy shows the same page does run and load them. The policy string is checked against `PLAN.md` §4's.

### Falling back to Arcadia

- **The app bundles Arcadia** beside the overlay as `dist/app/arcadia.js`, not `arcadia.json` as the plan said: the overlay's policy has `connect-src 'none'`, so it can't fetch a file, but it may run Margin's own scripts from its folder. The script sets one global with the package, and is loaded only when it's needed.
- **When:** the package is refused, missing or unreadable, or its `<m-page>` is under 200 × 150 pt or reaches outside the window (judged only in windows at least twice that size).
- **What shows:** Arcadia, drawn and said ready as usual, and a notice of the overlay's own, `theme-failed`. It doesn't name the theme (its name may be what's broken). Its buttons stay in the overlay: Settings opens Margin's Settings in that window, OK closes it. The copy can't push it and can't run its buttons (`isNoticeAction` refuses the overlay's own kinds).
- **`settings.theme` is kept,** so the copy's next package is tried again.
- **The log** says the theme's id and the kinds of what was wrong (`refused: 2 problem(s) in its theme.html`), never its files' text.

### Reading an imported theme

- **`ui/theme-import.js`** turns a folder's files or a `.margintheme` zip into the package every load takes, then checks it as every load does (`checkPackage`, `sanitizeTheme`) and refuses a built-in's id. Pure JS, so the overlay, the tests and `npm run theme:pack` share it.
- **The zip is read by hand, strictly:** one directory at the end, nothing before the first entry or between the entries and the directory, no zip64, no encryption, no links or special files, stored or deflated only, each local header agreeing with the directory, no two entries with one name in any case or sharing bytes, inflated with `DecompressionStream('deflate-raw')` while counting (never past what the entry says it holds, nor the kind's cap), and its CRC-32 checked. macOS's own zip and Finder's Compress make files it reads.
- **Folder rules:** at most 70 files, two folders deep, names of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` only (no `..`, no absolute paths, no backslashes, no look-alike letters), no two names differing by case (`Theme.json` beside `theme.json` is refused). Finder's `__MACOSX/` and `.DS_Store` are skipped; hidden folders (`.git/`) are left out by the readers of folders on disk.
- **What was removed is said by count and kind,** with the theme's own words taken out of the reasons ("2 declarations removed from theme.css: url() is not a bundled file…").
- **`npm run theme:pack <folder> [out]`** writes the zip (sorted, dated 1 January 2026, so the same folder makes the same file), after the same checks. It leaves out what a package doesn't hold (a built-in's `first-paint.css`, Arcadia's `theme.js`) and says so. All three built-ins go through it and back unchanged (`tests/theme-import.test.js`).
- **`MARGIN_THEMES`** takes `.margintheme` files too, read as an import is.

### Margin.app keeps the imported themes

- **For the whole Mac, outside the data sets:** `app/shell/ThemeStore.swift` keeps `~/Library/Application Support/Margin/themes/<id>.json` and `index.json`, written as `DataStore` writes. In a test the folder is a temporary one.
- **Copies get the index by a request (`req userThemes`), not through the data set** as the plan said. The themes aren't a profile's, so a per-profile collection would hold the same list once per profile and need merging for nothing. The request goes after each snapshot and on every change. The `userThemes` collection stays in the data set's list, unused.
- **The app chooses the package:** the stored one when a profile's `settings.theme` is in the index, the copy's otherwise. The copy still sends Arcadia for an id it doesn't ship, so an overlay always has something to draw.
- **Removing** a theme asks every linked copy that used it to go back to Arcadia. A copy that isn't linked keeps the old id in `settings.theme`: it gets Arcadia from its own package (the id isn't one it ships), and the next index tells its `updateSettings` the id is gone. Its `settings.themes[id]` is left: a few plain values, unused.
- **The picker** is `NSOpenPanel` (folders and any file; a chosen file must be named `.margintheme`), opened with the app activated and `.fullScreenAuxiliary`, `.moveToActiveSpace`, so it shows over full-screen Safari. The harness answers for it (`UserThemes.pick`).
- **Not built yet:** a plain first paint for a user theme's pages (they get Arcadia's frame before the overlay draws), the set-up window's "Use Arcadia in every profile".
- **`Shell.swift` changes by small hooks only:** one stored property, a `case` in `perform`, the theme chosen in the hello and on a new package, the index after a snapshot and the package checked after a settings change. The rest is in `ShellThemes.swift` and `ThemeStore.swift`.

### Settings for themes, and the preview

- **Settings › Theme** lists the built-ins, then the imported themes by name. In Margin.app: Import Theme… (with the last import's status under it), each imported theme as "“Name” 1.0.0 · by Author" with Remove, and the active theme's own settings under "Settings of “Name”" (after Margin's own settings: see the first review). Why Margin fell back to Arcadia shows under the theme choice.
- **A theme's own words in Margin's form** (its name, author, setting labels) are shown, as the plan proposed: capped at 40 characters, with bidi controls and zero-width characters taken out, inside Margin's words ("Settings of …", "Remove …"), and with `fromTheme` so a theme can mark them. They only ever save that theme's settings (`updateThemeSettings`, checked against its spec).
- **Lengths are number inputs** saved with their default's unit (`252` → `252px`). **Colours** are a new input, `m-input="setting-color"`: Margin makes it a colour well and sets its value; a colour that isn't `#rgb` or `#rrggbb` shows as black until changed. All three built-in themes draw it (Pixel's row is in its uncommitted files, beside the Pixel work).
- **Remove asks first** in Margin's prompt part: "Remove “Name”? Windows using it go back to Arcadia." Only its Remove button reaches the app.
- **The preview** draws the imported theme over the live window (its layout goes to the pages, so they fit it) under a bar of Margin's own: in the top layer (`popover="manual"`), in a closed shadow root, its host reset with `all: initial !important` both in its style attribute and from inside its shadow root (an inner `!important` beats the theme's), its `::before` and `::after` switched off, hung off `<html>` (a theme can hide `<body>`). A browser test throws a hostile stylesheet and a full-window element at it: it stays on top and takes the press. The bar's rectangle joins the overlay's hits, so the press reaches it. Escape cancels; 30 s with no answer cancels.
- **Use Theme** hands the checked package to the app as `encodeStoredTheme` makes it; the app stores it and sets the profile's theme. Cancel puts the package from before back (one the copy sent meanwhile is drawn instead).
- **Seen in the app's tests:** an off-screen overlay that took and gave back the keyboard gets no `resize` events afterwards in the harness (WebKit doesn't render it), so the import scenario runs after the window-size checks. On screen the overlay renders, so it doesn't apply there; worth a look in the real Safari check.

### Five profiles' restored full-screen windows: nothing bound, nothing drawn

- **What happened** (a real Safari log, 2026-11-06 21:24:30-21:25:30). Safari reopened with five profiles, one full-screen window each, all with the same bounds (0,33 1512×949), each on its own Space. No window was bound, so no overlay was drawn anywhere. Three things stopped it:
  - **A front change counted as a transition.** Safari came to the front (front window none, then 50775) 2.5 s after the Space slide that showed 50775. Nothing came on or went off screen, but the visible rule took it as a transition, so s-default's word "shown" (said as the slide began) was stale from then on: `no page with its bounds says it's shown since 21:24:49.786`.
  - **A silent page blocked it.** One profile's page never spoke (its tab not loaded). `unsure` blocked the shown page from binding: `safari:s-27f6…#199 said nothing of being hidden`.
  - **Focus moved lost to an offset.** After Margin updated, no page could speak, but s-default's focus change at 21:25:20.494 named its window. When it was weighed, a swipe had offset that window (3115,33): `doesn't fit window 50775`.
- **Transitions are windows coming on or going off screen** (`WindowBinder.update`), plus Space changes as before. The front window alone no longer counts: the browser coming to the front, or another on-screen window coming forward, shows and hides no page. A window come on screen starts a transition from the read before. It's folded into a Space change heard since that read, as the front change was. Windows only going off screen within `visibleLag` of the last change are its end (a slide: the new window on screen first, then the old one off). Further off, they're a transition of their own. A window missing from a read counts as it was. Each transition keeps the windows it took off screen (`went`).
- **A page that has said nothing doesn't block the shown one** once the pages have settled. The shown page binds its window even if other pages in the group never spoke (`visible == nil`), at `visibleLag` + `visibleQuiet` (1 s, new) after the last change's latest time (after Margin.app's first read if there was none). By then a page that newly said it was shown as its window slid away has said it's hidden and been heard. If every window the last change took off screen is bound, it binds at once: the page whose window went is known, and isn't this one. Still never: a page with an old word (shown before the change, or hidden and not yet settled) blocks as before. A silent page is never taken as hidden or as shown, so a window whose own page is silent isn't bound by the others' word. Every other gate stays: the browser in front, no link held, steady reads, the only window on screen with the bounds, every window with them reported (a Private window, or a profile without Margin, still blocks), one page alone saying it's shown since the change, and the hold. The log says `…said nothing yet (the pages settling after the last change)` while it waits, and the binding line ends `; X said nothing, the others hidden`.
- **Focus moved fits by settled bounds too**, as elimination does (`has`). A window offset for a moment in a slide still has its own bounds.
- **A test changed:** "one page saying nothing: nothing bound by the others' word while it's free" had the off-screen page silent and expected the shown page's window to stay unbound. Now the shown page's window is bound once the pages have settled, and not before (checked at 2.4 s and 3.6 s). The silent page being the one on screen still binds nothing, with its own case.
- **Tests** (`tools/app-tests/window-tests.swift`): the startup replay (five copies linking over 10 s, three hidden before they linked, one silent, the shown word said at the slide's start and heard 3 s late, Safari to the front 2.5 s after). The window on screen is bound within 0.6 s of the last copy reporting, and 30 seeded runs bring Safari to the front at various times. Then each Space in turn: each speaking page's window is bound within 1.5 s of its slide's end (2.5 s after the silent page's window, whose page can't say it's hidden), and the silent one by elimination once it's the only free window. The silent page on screen binds nothing. A free page that newly said it was shown as its window slid away, its hidden word 0.3, 0.9 or 1.5 s late, is never bound to the new window (with `visibleQuiet` at 0 the 1.5 s case binds wrong). And the focus change weighed while its window is offset. 10 of these checks fail against the binder before.
- **Not changed:** the copies, the link and the extension. Pages already say their state when they start and when asked. A page that hasn't loaded has no script to ask.

### Safari's windows from Accessibility events (2026-11-07)

- **What.** Margin hears Safari's own Accessibility events (an `AXObserver` on Safari's pid, public API, on a thread of its own: `SafariAX.watch`): a window created, focused, moved, resized, closed, and retitled while it had no title. Each one reads the window server at once (`Shell.axEvent` → `burst`), so a new window, a window going in or out of full screen, or a closed one is followed at once instead of at the next poll (0.25 s in front, 1 s behind). The poll stays as the safety net for a missed event.
- **The other Spaces' scan** (`_AXUIElementCreateWithRemoteToken`, the fragile call) is now made once per Safari launch, for windows already open on other Spaces, then only for a listed window still unknown 2 s later, at most every 5 s (`SafariAX.shouldScan`). An event gives every later window's element directly. Without the events, as before.
- **Full screen from Accessibility** (`AXKnown.fullScreen`): a window it read as not full screen skips SkyLight's Space reads in `placeAhead` and the covers. One it read as full screen is still checked with SkyLight, because entering full screen says so before the window is in its own Space.
- **Not changed:** the profile names (still Safari's files), the handoff's Space reads, parking.
- **Tests** (`tools/app-tests/window-tests.swift` `axEvents`): the scan policy with and without events (a window never found: about 12 scans a minute instead of 120), and what's kept (an event naming a profile without a read, untitled then titled, closed, out of full screen, no profile names, only listed windows). Not checked on real Safari by me: Safari wasn't running and I don't open it in your profiles.

### The sidebar missing after a swipe: the own-Space fallback at every launch (2026-11-07)

- **What was seen:** "sometimes i don't see our ui at all after i switch using swipe", from before the Accessibility events.
- **Why** (the real log, 2026-11-07): at every Safari launch (10:44:49, 10:52:17), 5 ms after the first overlay was shown, "an overlay placed in its window's Space isn't on screen with it: overlays join every Space again". From then on, for the whole run of Safari, an overlay isn't kept in its window's Space: each swipe put the sidebar away while the window slid ("its window doesn't fill its display") and showed it again 1.5–5 s later.
- **The race:** `checkOwnSpace` was asked on every read where the overlay wasn't shown before, even when `show` failed because its page wasn't drawn yet (about 0.6 s at launch). Each one judged 250 ms later. The one due just after the real show judged the overlay 5 ms after it was ordered in, before macOS lists it as on screen. Now a check is asked only for an overlay that was shown, and it judges only an overlay shown since before it was asked (`OverlayController.shownAt`).
- **A second path** (10:55:41): an overlay put away as suspect, then correctly placed in its window's Space ahead of a visit, and 314 ms later the old suspicion still made every overlay join every Space. A suspicion is now dropped when its overlay was shown again since (`Shell.ownSpaceCleared`).
- **Tests:** `tools/app-tests/e2e-overlays.swift`: macOS lists a just-shown overlay on screen 150 ms later, and a new Safari's overlay page draws after several reads. This failed before the fix ("fell back: true") and passes after. `window-tests.swift` `ownSpaceJudge`: the placed-again case failed before ("kept") and passes after.

### The window module, step 1: the window map and its trace (2026-11-07)

- **Why.** Reported: layouts late, one on a Desktop where Safari isn't, and more to come with a second display ("create a separate module that would do all the window related stuff and it know what window is where"). The plan has four steps, each merged on its own: (1) the map and a trace, (2) a planner (a pure function: map → where each overlay should be), (3) a placer that carries out the plan and checks each overlay against the next map, (4) the switch, parking and displays on it.
- **The map** (`app/shell/WindowMap.swift`): every window Margin cares about as one snapshot. That's the browsers' windows and Margin's own (overlays, covers, catchers), each with its bounds, on screen, its order, its display (by its centre, from the screens' frames), its Spaces, and, for Safari's, its profile and full screen from Accessibility. It also holds every display with its frame, the Space it shows and its full-screen Spaces. Each display has its own current Space: there's no single active Space in it. It's fed from `Shell.track` (the read it already makes), the Space and display change notifications, and Accessibility. Spaces cost one SkyLight read per window, so a window's are read when it's new, moved, on or off screen, after a Space or display change, and at least every second. Nothing decides from the map yet.
- **The trace** (`app/shell/WindowTrace.swift`, DEV: `MarginWindowTrace` NO turns it off): JSON lines in `~/Library/Application Support/Margin/traces/`, with the map (whole every 30 s, else what changed), the copies' windows (state, bounds, focus), the overlays (shown, over which window, own Space, frame) and events (Space and display changes, links, Accessibility, switches by id). Numbers and Margin's keys only: no title, address or profile name. 5 MB per file, the newest 5 kept. `WindowTrace.load`/`replay` rebuild the maps, so a real session becomes a test.
- **Tests** (`window-tests.swift` `windowMap`): two displays with their own current Spaces, owners, displays by centre, Spaces read (another app's not), Accessibility's profile and full screen, a swipe on one display, no Space read under a second when nothing moved, a close, a read with no list, no SkyLight (unknown, not guessed), and the trace written, read back and replayed to the same maps, with no title in it.

### A sidebar left on the Desktop after a switch: kept in its window's Space (2026-11-07)

- **What was seen** (recording 11:33:02): after switching profiles and swiping to the Desktop, Margin's sidebar was there, over Finder, with no Safari.
- **Why** (the real window trace, the first use of it): the switch brought Personal's parked window back into a new full-screen Space (3042 → 3046), and macOS removed the old one. The sidebar, kept hidden in the old Space while its window was parked, was moved to the Desktop (Space 1) by macOS. Shown again over its window, it stayed in Space 1: not over Safari after the switch, and on the Desktop after the swipe there. The same happened after an earlier switch (3038). Nothing checked that a sidebar is in its window's Space. The own-Space check only looks at "on screen", and only once a Space change has settled for a second.
- **Now:** each read, a shown sidebar in its window's own Space is compared with its window's Spaces (`Shell.keepInWindowSpace`, `Shell.spaceToJoin`). If its window is on screen, in one Space that's showing, and the sidebar is in another, it's moved there with the Space bridge, at most once a second for each. The Spaces are read from SkyLight there and then when the sidebar was just shown, or when the map has it off screen while its window is on.
- **Tests:** `window-tests.swift` `overlaySpace`: the rule's cases, and **the real session replayed** from `tests/fixtures/traces/2026-11-07-sidebar-on-desktop.jsonl` (the trace cut to the sidebar and its window, numbers only). It checks that the sidebar was in Space 1 while its window showed in 3046, and that the rule moves it into 3046 and nowhere else. `WindowTrace.replayWithOverlays` gives each replayed map with the overlays' states.

### The window module, step 2: the planner (2026-11-07)

- **What.** `app/shell/OverlayPlanner.swift`: what each overlay should do on a read (made or not, put away, concealed, left in its Space, placed ahead, suspected, moved into its window's Space, left to slide, shown), decided from facts only (`OverlayFacts`) by a pure function. `Shell.track` gathers the facts (the copy's window, the switch, the binding, the window server's read, the overlay as it is, the window map's Spaces), asks, and carries the decision out. Each rule has a test (`window-tests.swift` `overlayPlanner`), and the real traces replay through it.
- **The same decisions as before.** The first version is Shell.track's overlay loop moved over: the same rules in the same order, with the same words in the log. The app's 449 end-to-end checks are the proof.
- **The first new rule** (from the real trace, 11:33:03): an overlay kept in its window's own Space whose Spaces the map knows, and they aren't its window's single Space, is moved there at once with the Space bridge (`.join`). Before, it was left as it was, and if it was on screen it was suspected only once a Space change had settled for a second: the sidebar sat on the Desktop for that second. Not while a switch moves its window, and not without the bridge. The replay test failed before the rule (`.reveal`) and passes after (`.join(3046)`).
- **Next:** more rules move from the shell's checks into the planner (the on-screen Space check, the own-Space suspicion and its fallback, which the Spaces make unneeded when they're known), then the placer (step 3) takes the carrying out.
- **The Space checks moved in** (2026-11-07, later). The check after a show (`OverlayPlanner.spaceToJoin`, carried out by `Shell.keepInWindowSpace` with Spaces read right then) is a planner rule now. The own-Space suspicion ("on screen while its window isn't") and the check a moment after a first show, with their fallback of every overlay in every Space, are now guesses for when the Spaces can't be read or used (no SkyLight, no bridge, the harness). With the Spaces known, an overlay out of its window's Space is moved there, alone, and a same-Spaces "on screen" read is taken as stale. The harness has no bridge, so its own-Space checks run as before (449 end-to-end checks unchanged).

### The window module, step 3: the placer checks each placement (2026-11-07)

- **What.** `app/shell/OverlayPlacer.swift`. Each show records what was asked (`PlacedOverlay`: the overlay's window, the window it's over, the frame, the window's bounds then). `Shell.checkPlacements` then checks it on each read's map (`PlacementCheck.check`), once 0.2 s have passed, only while its window is on screen at those bounds (not while it moves or slides) and not while a switch moves it. In order: (1) not in its window's single showing Space → moved there (`joinSpace`); (2) not on screen while its window is → ordered in again over it (at most every 2 s); (3) not at the frame asked → said (every 30 s at most). A fix comes on the second map in a row that's wrong. Each fix goes in the log and the trace.
- **Before,** a shown overlay was taken as on screen over its window. One that macOS left in another Space, ordered out, or put behind stayed so until something else moved.
- **Not its order against its window.** In the real trace an overlay in front of its window read 136 in the window list against the window's 1: the list's order (`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo`, every window) isn't front to back between Margin's windows and Safari's. (`WindowMatcher.stackedAbove` reads the same orders: to look at.)
- **Tests** (`window-tests.swift` `placementCheck`): each check, the grace, the two maps in a row, a moving, sliding or off-screen window not judged, no bridge, and the real session replayed at a read every 0.25 s (a trace holds a map only when something changed). The sidebar left in the Desktop's Space is caught and moved into 3046 first.

A probe the same day with Safari in front read 101 against 126 (right). `WindowMatcher.stackedAbove` reads that order, so a wrong "behind" ordered the overlay in again on every read, and held a switch's R4 ("B's overlay above B") back.

### The same sidebar through a profile switch (2026-11-07)

- **Why** (the report: "since it's gonna switch in the exact same place, it should technically look the same"). A switch showed the target window's own sidebar: another page, loaded and placed on its own ("B's overlay not framed in 200 ms" in almost every switch of the log; once in the wrong Space). The sidebar on screen already drew the target space and the switch's cover.
- **Now.** As the freeze starts (A's sidebar showing the cover and the target space, B not shown yet), A's sidebar is handed to B (`Handoff.handOver` → `Shell.handOverOverlay`). The two controllers swap keys (`OverlayController.rekey`), and each page, if drawn, takes its new window's hello in place (`rekey` push → `host-app.js` resets its window, state, mode, windows, across and iCloud Tabs and draws again; `overlay.js` applies held pushes and mounts the theme if that profile's differs). What the shell kept of each for a window is forgotten (`forgetOverlayState`). The sidebar is put away under the freeze. The next read shows it over B once B is in place, which orders it into B's Space (checked by `keepInWindowSpace` and the placer) and tells its page it's shown, and its `framed` is R4. B's own sidebar, if it had one, is A's now and goes out with A's (`outA`).
- **When not.** Without a freeze (the hand-over would be seen), when A's sidebar isn't shown and drawn, or when B's is already shown (a full-screen target whose sidebar is kept in its own Space, already drawn). A window made by the switch: at R2, once B is known. Once per switch.
- **Tests.** `handoff-tests.swift`: handed under the freeze before A's goes out, the switch otherwise the same; none without a freeze. `e2e-profiles.swift` switch 1: the sidebar kept (`overlays[k8] === o7`, its key B's), B's own A's now and hidden, its page not loaded again; the checks that held "A's sidebar" as an object now look it up by window. `ui-host-app.test.js`: a rekey takes the new window, state and mode.

### A pinched page and the docked inspector (2026-11-07)

- **What was seen** (recording 14:00:52): the layout late beside the docked Web Inspector, and "A problem repeatedly occurred" after opening and closing it a few times.
- **The sidebar drawn in a corner.** The new timings in the log (the page's resize, its word, its copy hearing it, Margin drawing: `viewportTimes`, `Shell.viewportDelay`) showed hops of 10–60 ms. They also showed areas of 504 × 316 in a 1512 × 949 window: a third each way. Measured in WebKit off screen, a 3× pinch makes `innerWidth`/`innerHeight` read 504 × 316 (visualViewport 504 × 316.33 at scale 3). The page script took that as Safari taking most of the window: Margin drew its sidebar in a third of it, and the page's box lost its left inset. Now `shared/app-link.js` `unpinchedSize` gives the area before any pinch: as it is unpinched, else scaled back from the larger of the inner and visual sizes. It's used for the area told to Margin and for the page's box. Where the area starts isn't learnt from a pointer event while pinched.
- **Tests:** `link.test.js` (WebKit's measured numbers; the box unchanged by a pinch). WebKit host `pinch-native`: a linked page pinched 3× by Safari (gestures not Margin's) keeps its box and tells Margin the whole window. It fails on the old script with `{x: 800, y: 534, width: 400, height: 266}`. It needs the host to tell WebKit the window's frame (new op `windowFrame`, only this scenario: other scenarios keep outerWidth 0 as before).
- **The crash** is Safari's: every WebContent crash on the development Mac since 2026-11-05 (11 reports) is `JSC::TypeLocationCache::getTypeLocation` ← `CodeBlock::finishCreation`, JavaScriptCore's type profiler, as a function compiles right after the inspector opens or closes. That Mac's Inspector settings don't have type information on. Whether Margin's scripts make it likelier is open: to be tried with Margin off in a profile.

### The type-profiler crash: its trigger found (2026-11-07)

- An A/B in real Safari: with Margin off in a profile, opening and closing the Web Inspector many times never crashed. With it on, the page crashed after 8–10 times.
- The trigger is a Web Inspector setting. The Inspector turns JavaScriptCore's type profiler on as it connects, and off as it closes, only when "Show type information" (`com.apple.WebInspector.show-javascript-type-information`) or code coverage is on: WebInspectorUI's Main.js, `RuntimeManager.initializeTarget`. In that Safari it's `true` (the Inspector's own local storage, UTF-16, which a plain-text search missed). Safari 27.2 then crashes compiling a function across a toggle (`TypeLocationCache::getTypeLocation`). Margin makes that likelier, because each toggle resizes the page and Margin runs a burst of page code then.
- The fix is that setting. In the Inspector's Sources tab, with a script open, the "Show/Hide type information" button: off. Margin doesn't write Safari's settings. The WebKit host can't dock its Inspector, so it can't reproduce Safari's resize; the experiment was dropped. The host keeps a crash counter (a web content process ending is logged; op `noCrash`).

The page-world box no longer scales at <html>, and the page's area stays right under Safari's pinch (`unpinchedSize`, above).
- Removed: `content/pinch.js`; the gesture guard's `own` mode, `onPinch`, `onWheelFirst` and its gesturechange/gestureend handlers (`shared/gestures.js`); `trackpad.js`'s pinch routing and pan; `page-link.js` `setZoom`; `page/box.js`'s zoom sheet, `setZoom` and the `scale` field in its bridge messages (an older content script's are ignored); `Margin.content.pinched`.
- Kept: the gesture guard (no swipe back/forward, no all-tabs pinch, no bounce), the `blockGestures` setting (its label no longer says "pinch zooms the page"), and pull-to-refresh and swipe, which now stand aside while Safari has the page magnified (`visualViewport.scale`).
- Tests: `gestures.test.js` (only the first gesture event is looked at, `block` and `native`), WebKit host `pinch-box` rewritten (Safari's magnification on a boxed page, the box in place, the area told as the whole window, the all-tabs pinch cancelled), `pinch` and `pinch-native` unchanged. README, SPEC (file list) and TESTING updated.
